title: The X Files Darkness Falls
segments: How many of them might be out there, filling the sky, covering the trees, getting hungrier
and hungrier.
Let's just hope they make these things well until I warn," said Muir, still holding
on to the light bulb.
Don is a long way away.
Scully didn't even try to go to sleep.
She was trembling too hard.
There was only one way she knew to calm down.
She had to get back to work.
She lay on her bunk and thought about the case.
Suddenly a thought struck her.
She got up and went to her backpack.
She took a glass jar from it and set it on the table.
I thought so, she said to herself.
She turned and said to the others,
come here, take a look at this.
Mulder and Moore joined her.
They looked at the glowing dots of green light inside the jar.
They were about a dozen.
They flew furiously fast as if struggling to escape.
I collected these in the forest from the cocoon we found.
They appear to be like fireflies.
If that's the case, the light they give off comes from waste from their bodies.
When the waste hits the air, it produces a glow, in this case, a green glow.
Right, a chemical reaction from instant oxidation.
Except, these aren't fireflies, said Mulder.
Squinting into the jar, fireflies don't look like tiny spiders.
Biders, fireflies don't make cocoons.
Fireflies don't suck the life out of you.
That must be how they make the cocoons.
After they feed, they have to get rid of waste.
It mixes with their juices.
They squirt it out.
It hits the air with a glow,
and it turns to strands of greasy gray fiber.
Judging from the cocoon we found,
they're hungry little devils.
They must suck every last bit of nourishment from their prey.
Ray, you'd be hungry too if you hadn't eaten for centuries. They're making up for lost
time now.
I wonder how many there are. No telling. But I'd guess in the millions, there had to be
that many to take care of thirty loggers. Trouble is, that may not be the worst news.
What is? said Scully.
I have an idea they're multiplying by the minute, said Mulder. The more they eat, the
faster they breed. When they found those thirty loggers they hit the jackpot. It was a feast
for them, and it must have set off a population explosion. Insects are like that. That's why
they outnumber us by so much. But they've never eaten humans before.
It's always a first time. And this one could mean the end of human life. Other species have
disappeared in the past. The dinosaurs, the mastodons, were still not sure why. But we
We do know there were volcanic eruptions that disturbed the Earth.
They could have set off a plague like this one.
It could be our turn now to be victims.
We also know meteors from outer space have hit the Earth.
They could have brought deadly life forms with them.
Whatever their origin, these insects are a threat to human life.
And they're a threat to our lives, for sure, said Moore.
At that moment, the electric light flickered.
In the distance, the hum of the generator faltered.
Oh God!" said Scully, her fists clenching. Cold sweat beaded her skin, and her mind was
a picture of the bugs swarming, closing in on them, feasting on them. Then the light
studied, so did the hum of the generator. Scully wiped the sweat off her forehead.
Maybe we'll make it through the night. Said Mulder.
Maybe. Said Moore.
But then what? It's over a day's hike out of the forest. We could never make it before
nightfall. By now the bugs must be ranging all over the woods looking for food if they
find us outside after dark we're dead.
Maybe somebody heard our radio call said Mulder. Help could be on the way. You sent that call
hours ago. Help would be here by now."
Stands to reason. The Forest Service has choppers. So does the lumber company. While I'm not giving
up on spinny, he gave me his word he'd come back to get us.
